lead.title: Biomatter raises $18M Series A led by Astanor to design custom enzymes with AI, all the way to mRNA vaccine manufacturing
lead.deck: The Vilnius company, led by co-founder Laurynas Karpus, closed an oversubscribed round led by Astanor with existing investors UVC Partners, Inventure and Metaplanet; it has already designed enzymes for AstraZeneca, BASF, Sanofi and Tereos, including a methylase that works without SAM, a costly additive in mRNA vaccine manufacturing. The money funds a 2,000 m² design and testing facility in Vilnius (opening in 2027) to cut cycles from weeks to days, plus a commercial push in the US — a picks-and-shovels bet on biomanufacturing from an under-covered geography.

milestone.title: European Commission approves Zeydovio (glepaglutide), Zealand Pharma's GLP-2 analog for short bowel syndrome
milestone.summary: Glepaglutide, a long-acting GLP-2 analog injected twice weekly via a ready-to-use autoinjector, is authorised in the EU, Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway. In the pivotal EASE-1 trial (106 patients), 65.7% of patients dosed twice weekly cut their parenteral support by at least 20% at 24 weeks versus 38.9% on placebo, and five of them came off it entirely.
milestone.why: This is an approval without a commercial partner: Zealand is now looking for a global licensee for the launch, while the EASE-5 trial must deliver the confirmatory evidence the FDA requires. An approved rare-disease asset available for licensing is exactly the kind of deal watched by funds that back commercialisation NewCos.

brefsEurope.title: University of Basel spin-off 201 Therapeutics wins CHF 150,000 from Venture Kick for liver cancer
brefsEurope.summary: Founded by Sandro Nuciforo (CEO), Fredrik Trulsson, Markus Heim and Emmanuel Meyer, the company is developing two series of small molecules that selectively kill liver cancer cells, screened on mini-tumours grown from patient biopsies. The money will go to lead optimisation and first in vivo efficacy data.

brefsEurope.title: Gubra ousts CEO Markus Rohrwild and hands the reins to co-CEOs Kristian Borbos and Zoë Johnson
brefsEurope.summary: The board removed the CEO on November 10, two weeks after unveiling a 2030 strategy (grow from 4 to 8-10 clinical assets and launch 2-3 ventures); the CFO and the head of ventures/BD take charge while keeping their roles. A signal to watch for new company spin-outs from the group's peptide platform.

brefsEurope.title: Novo Nordisk files etavopivat, an oral pyruvate kinase activator, with the FDA and EMA in sickle cell disease
brefsEurope.summary: The filing rests on the Phase 2/3 HIBISCUS trial (about 440 patients aged 12+): 27% fewer vaso-occlusive crises over 52 weeks and a first crisis delayed by about four months versus placebo; decisions are expected in 2027. A comparable for European hemoglobinopathy biotechs up against one-time gene therapies.

brefsEurope.title: November CHMP: seven new medicines recommended, including AstraZeneca's baxdrostat, and a confirmed refusal for Zevra's arimoclomol
brefsEurope.summary: The committee backed Baxfendy (baxdrostat, hypertension) and eleven label extensions, including Gazyvaro in lupus; on re-examination it upheld the refusal of Meplyffa (arimoclomol, Zevra Denmark) in Niemann-Pick disease type C, a drug already approved in the US. A reminder for investors: an FDA nod in a rare disease does not guarantee European access.

brefsEurope.title: Cellectis plans to cut up to 70% of its workforce as it pivots to in vivo gene editing
brefsEurope.summary: The allogeneic CAR-T pioneer is shutting down lasme-cel and eti-cel and focusing its $149M cash (runway into 2H 2028) on HEAL-101, an APOC3 base editor (first human data in 2H 2027 via an investigator-initiated trial in China), and HEAL-201, a PCSK9 epigenetic editor. A sign that allogeneic cell therapy has lost investor favour to in vivo approaches.

brefsIntl.title: Wave Life Sciences shows at ObesityWeek that its INHBE siRNA cuts visceral fat while preserving lean mass
brefsIntl.summary: WVE-007, a single-dose GalNAc siRNA, lowers activin E by 82-88%; at 240 mg, visceral fat and waist circumference fell at one year with no loss of lean mass. The Phase 2a (BMI 35-50) will report six-month data in 2027: a direct comparable for Europe's next-generation obesity players.

word.definition: The craft of modifying — or building from scratch — an enzyme, the proteins that speed up chemical reactions, so it cleanly makes a useful molecule (an mRNA vaccine ingredient, a drug substance, a reagent) where conventional chemistry is slow, costly or polluting.

parts.label: Sequence
parts.role: the recipe: the chain of amino acids that sets the enzyme's shape and therefore its activity

parts.label: Predictive model
parts.role: the brain: an AI trained on lab data that proposes the most promising mutations

parts.label: Test bench
parts.role: the judge: lab screening that measures activity, stability and purity, then feeds the model

how.t: Define the target reaction and its industrial constraints: temperature, solvent, no costly cofactor, impurities to avoid.
AI models generate or mutate candidate sequences — where classic directed evolution randomly tested thousands of variants.
The best variants are produced and measured; results retrain the model, and each cycle shortens the next until the enzyme is ready for industrial scale.

word.why: Biomanufacturing of mRNA, peptides and oligonucleotides needs enzymes nature does not provide: it is a picks-and-shovels market that wins whichever drug comes out on top. AI is cutting design from months to weeks, and Europe's leaders (Biomatter, Cradle, EnginZyme) already work with AstraZeneca, Sanofi or Novo Nordisk. Diligence points: ability to scale industrially, ownership of enzymes designed for clients, and business model (licence, royalty or supply).

startups.name: Biomatter
startups.use: Designs custom enzymes with AI (including a SAM-free methylase for mRNA) for AstraZeneca, BASF, Sanofi and Tereos; $18M Series A led by Astanor in November 2026.

startups.name: Cradle
startups.use: Generative AI software that helps R&D teams design proteins and enzymes; customers include Novo Nordisk, J&J and Novonesis, $73M Series B led by IVP.

startups.name: EnginZyme
startups.use: Cell-free biocatalysis: patented with Ajinomoto Bio-Pharma an enzymatic process to make pseudouridine, a key mRNA vaccine ingredient, without the alpha impurity.

startups.name: Enzymit
startups.use: Computational enzyme design platform for cell-free bioproduction; $10M Series A led by Grove Ventures and Khosla Ventures.
